transcript: Most people think saving money means giving up everything they enjoy. It does not. It starts with knowing where your money goes. For one month, write down every rupee you spend: rent, groceries, the bus fare, the late-night snack. At the end of the month, sort it into three groups: needs, wants and savings. You will be surprised how much slips away on small things nobody remembers buying. Next, pay yourself first. On payday, move a fixed amount into a separate savings account before you spend anything else. Even five percent of your salary adds up. Then build an emergency fund that covers three months of expenses, so a broken phone or a hospital bill does not push you into debt. Cook at home a few more nights each week, cancel the subscriptions you forgot about, and compare prices before every big purchase. Small habits, repeated every day, turn into real security. Start this month, and in a year you will not recognise your bank balance.
selection_rule: Per scene: (1) statistics -> animated stat card. (2) Stock candidates from category-suited sources are scored with CLIP (image vs scene visual plan + narration, minus penalty for negative/avoid terms); unsafe candidates (avoid list, faces when avoided, AI for people/brands/sensitive) are removed. (3) Global assignment takes the highest (scene, clip) pairs first, each clip used once, if score >= tau=0.24. (4) If a scene's best stock score < tau+0.03 and AI is allowed, an AI image is generated and wins only if its CLIP score >= stock + 0.02. (5) Otherwise the best unused clip within 0.03 of tau, else a text card.
